Plot treated and synthetic control trajectories

Source: R/plot.R
sdid_plot.Rd

Plots the treated and synthetic control trajectories of an sdid() result, along with the time weights, which show which pre-treatment periods were most informative for predicting post-treatment outcomes among the controls.

Usage

sdid_plot(
  estimates,
  treated.name = "treated",
  control.name = "synthetic control",
  spaghetti.units = c(),
  spaghetti.matrices = NULL,
  lambda.comparable = FALSE,
  overlay = 0,
  lambda.plot.scale = 3,
  effect.curvature = 0.3,
  line.width = 0.5,
  point.size = 1,
  onset.alpha = 0.8,
  spaghetti.line.width = 0.2,
  spaghetti.label.size = 2,
  spaghetti.line.alpha = 0.3,
  spaghetti.label.alpha = 0.5,
  alpha.multiplier = NULL,
  style = c("minimal", "effects"),
  lambda.axis = TRUE,
  x.breaks = NULL,
  y.breaks = NULL
)

Arguments

estimates

The result of an sdid object or a list of sdid estimates. For a staggered sdid result, each adoption period is plotted in a stacked panel.

treated.name

A string conveying the name of the treated curve that appears in the legend. Defaults to "treated".

control.name

A string conveying the name of the control curve that appears in the legend. Defaults to 'synthetic control'.

spaghetti.units

A list of units to plot individually alongside the treatment and control curves. Defaults to the empty list.

spaghetti.matrices

A list of matrices, one per estimate, of extra trajectories to plot. Each row is a trajectory, one column per period, and row names are used as labels.

lambda.comparable

Logical argument where if TRUE, the lambda weight axis is scaled to range from 0 to 1. Useful for when comparing across stacked panels. Defaults to FALSE.

overlay

Between 0 and 1. Shifts the synthetic control toward the treated line by this fraction of their pre-treatment gap, which makes it easier to see whether they move in parallel. Defaults to 0 (no shift). A vector of values can be animated with plotly.

lambda.plot.scale

Height of the time-weight band: the range of the trajectories divided by this number. Defaults to 3.

effect.curvature

Curvature of the effect arrow in the effects style.

line.width

Width of the trajectory lines.

point.size

Size of the points in the effects style.

onset.alpha

Opacity of the red dashed line that marks treatment.

spaghetti.line.width, spaghetti.label.size, spaghetti.line.alpha, spaghetti.label.alpha

Width, label size and opacity of the spaghetti trajectories and their labels.

alpha.multiplier

One number per estimate that scales its opacity, to emphasize some estimates over others.

style

The plot's style, "minimal" (the default) or "effects". See Details.

lambda.axis

Logical argument where if TRUE, each panel with a time weights' band shows the band's scale on a right-hand axis. Defaults to TRUE.

x.breaks, y.breaks

Optional tick positions for the time and outcome axes (numbers, or dates for a date axis). The axes are extended to the outermost ticks if needed. With stacked panels, y.breaks applies to every panel.

Value

A ggplot object, which can be extended with +.

Details

Two plotting styles are available: "minimal" and "effects". The default, style = "minimal", plots both trajectories in black, with the treated line solid and the synthetic control dashed. The time weights are plotted as a gray band with their scale on a right-hand axis, and a red dashed line marks treatment. style = "effects" adds a diff-in-diff diagram of the treatment effect and fades the trajectory lines.

A staggered sdid() result is drawn as one panel per cohort, stacked in a column and labeled by adoption period. A list of results is drawn the same way, one panel each. To change the axis ticks, use x.breaks and y.breaks rather than adding your own scale, which would drop the time-weight axis.

Requires ggplot2.
